attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction on his Substack, under his 'High confidence' heading. It is his own words, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The main claim uses unhedged 'will' under 'High confidence', so it is a scored forecast. 'Possibly' qualifies only the narrow-use exception, which the normalised claim keeps. The 2025 horizon is preserved.

contract.note: Reading 'endlessly hyped' as prominent company promotion across 2025, and 'far from reliable' as failing a large share of realistic multi-step tasks, follows the speaker's words. Narrow uses are excepted. Given a 30% best-agent completion rate, any reasonable reading gives the same result.

evidence.note: OpenAI CEO, January 2025, promoting agents joining the workforce. This is a company disclosure, but the hype limb concerns promotion itself, so the statement is evidence that hype occurred. It says nothing about reliability.
OpenAI CEO, June 2025, saying agents do real cognitive work. Shows promotion continuing mid-year. Not a reliability test.

Independent academic benchmark, v3 dated September 2025. The best agent completed only 30% of realistic workplace tasks autonomously, and long-horizon tasks were beyond reach. This fits 'far from reliable' for general-purpose agents. It is a preprint.

output.rationale: The horizon ended 2025-12-31. The leading AI company's CEO promoted agents as transformative in January and June 2025, meeting the hype limb. An independent September 2025 benchmark found the best agent completing only 30% of realistic multi-step work tasks, meeting the unreliability limb. The packet holds no counterevidence. The lack of late-2025 tests and of narrow-use measurement does not undercut the general claim.
